synopsis: ISO/PRF 21815-5 addresses collision risk from motions beyond ordinary forward/reverse travel and rotation: articulation, four-wheel steering, reversing towed trailers, skid or differential turning, counter-rotation, telescopic movement, and vertical movement, with interventions including speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition [f2176, f1136, f2177]. It specifically distinguishes stationary articulation, where the rear swings without machine travel, from steering during travel [f6038, f13740]. The first-edition project was approved on 27 September 2024; a BSI comment draft was dated 6 June 2025, the DIS ballot closed on 30 August 2025, and the FDIS was approved on 25 June 2026 [f2173, f2174, f2175]. As reported in October 2026, it had been at proof stage 50.20 since 9 September, with publication scheduled or expected for November 2026 rather than confirmed [f10904, f15154, f10905, f5075]. The corpus reports no statistical acceptance target, sample-size rules or simulation-credibility rules from Part 5; its testing requirements were not reviewed, acceptance of simulation evidence was not found, and final content remained uncertain [f324, f6749, f2673, f11237, f2863]. Planning recommendations therefore include tracking the draft, maintaining a standards watch and re-baselining before design freeze, while encoding its motion risk areas as machine-scaled scenario geometry [f6748, f15058, f6770].
